officialSources.observation: Beirut Urban Lab says its database, developed with CNRS, includes municipal Beirut property boundaries and lot numbers, with downloadable data under ODbL.
Beirut Urban Lab describes free downloadable updated BBED layers and states ODbL attribution requirements.

Beirut Urban Lab polygon layer; safe native fields include OBJECTID, CadastralID, Mohafaza, Kadaa, ArabicName, EnglishName, Cadastral_NewEng, DataSource and DateCreated. Layer metadata reports dataLastEditDate 2026-04-22; user/editor field CreatedBy omitted.
Publisher-linked Experience app references web map e74d5dc120dc4ac6bbe3fb22976686c7, whose Parcels of Beirut layer is forDameg FeatureServer/1.
Parcel_Output: description explicitly defines PID as cadastral district abbreviation plus parcel number, e.g. Ai_133. Geometry is separate individual land parcels.

requests.method: GET ArcGIS REST bounded query via curl
requests.outcome: Returned three Polygon geometries in municipal Beirut bbox; query requested OBJECTID and geometry only. Response exceededTransferLimit=true, but this bounded response contained exactly three features.
Primary publisher page read: property boundaries and parcel numbers, 2019 survey update, linked download/map platform and ODbL notice.
Parcels of Beirut references the tested forDameg layer.
Polygon parcel layer with PID/native district-and-lot reference, OBJECTID_1 transport identity, EPSG:32636 native.

registryBasis: The publisher-linked municipal Beirut cadastral basemap returns individual parcel polygons and district/lot references. This establishes local cadastral geometry; legal registration, ownership, and currentness are not established by the research copy.

sourceCandidate.publisher: Beirut Urban Lab / American University of Beirut, with CNRS
sourceCandidate.nativeIdentity: PID: district abbreviation plus parcel number; OBJECTID_1 is transport identity
sourceCandidate.scope: Bounded municipal Beirut parcels; publisher describes a basemap updated to its 2019 survey. This is a research basemap, not a legal title service.

coverageAssessment.verifiedOpenScope: 89 complete district-and-parcel PID references in 13 Beirut cells. Publisher describes a 2019-survey basemap; current legal registration and citywide completeness unverified. Two unchanged boundary slivers are under 0.31 m², 0.076% of the smaller parcel and 4.3 cm wide.

purpose: City parcel geometry and registry/cadastre research; registry evidence and publicly retrievable vector geometry are assessed independently.
